text: Define the memory-charging rule for a MemoryObject whose ownership moves between ResourceDomains (charge follows owner; a borrow never double-charges) and test budget enforcement across a transfer.
Define mapping of a Capability<File> into a MemoryObject: coherence with Write Operations, an msync equivalent, and interaction with copy-on-write snapshots.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Prototype MemoryObject ownership transfer over candidate backings (shmem/memfd, dma-buf, dedicated native object) and measure transfer cost for 4 KB and 64 MB objects including TLB shootdown.
rationale: Zero-copy dataflow is only real if transfer is cheaper than copying at realistic sizes.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether ownership transfer is enforced (kernel unmaps the sender) or advisory (sender promises not to touch), with the measured enforcement cost attached.
rationale: Enforced transfer gives security guarantees but may cost more than a copy for small objects; the semantics must be fixed before SDK types are designed.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether dma-buf becomes the underlying implementation for DMA- and GPU-compatible MemoryObjects and demonstrate a NIC-to-GPU zero-copy path on target hardware.
rationale: Reusing dma-buf keeps mature GPU drivers working; the end-to-end demo proves the §17 dataflow is achievable rather than aspirational.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the per-component page-table and huge-page policy for MemoryObjects and immutable package mappings after measuring startup and TLB effects.
rationale: The sub-20 ms startup target depends on how cheaply verified immutable pages can be mapped and shared.

text: Define and implement MemoryObject as the fundamental large-data abstraction.
